newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN CORN BUYERS SIDELINED ON USDA, WATCH CHINA.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN CORN BUYERS SIDELINED ON USDA, WATCH CHINA.

text.p: Japanese corn buyers are seen hesitant to buy U.S. corn until at least next week, in the wake of the surge in U.S. grain prices on Tuesday triggered by bullish USDA crop reports, traders said on Wednesday.
"Local importers are expected to return to the market early next week (after the Japanese summer holidays this week)," a corn trader at a major trade house said.
"But they'll probably remain sidelined and keep watching market direction at least until the end of next week, given the surprising rally last night," he said.
Japanese buyers have so far covered up to 40 percent of their demand for U.S. corn during the October-December quarter traders said.
Some feed maker officials said that depending on prices they may turn to Chinese corn, following surge in U.S. prices.
"We have usually shifted to Chinese corn in the past when U.S. corn prices rose," a senior official of a major feed maker in western Japan said.
"But Chinese exporters are now quick to raise offer prices when the U.S. corn market rises. We're watching how China reacts to the overnight price rally in Chicago," the official said.
On Tuesday, the USDA estimated U.S. 1997 corn production would be around 9.276 billion bushels, sharply below its forecast of 9.7 billion in July.
The September corn futures on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) ended the 12-cent limit up, at $2.61-3/4 per bushel.
